rubrics.criterion: After the repair, the read-only computed field families (the SizeOf* fields and Pointer* fields, across every width, their shared base classes, and the standalone 64-bit variants) no longer carry a value-mutator set() they do not use; the field contracts separate value-mutation from buffer shape so these owners depend only on what they support.
rubrics.rationale: The read-only computed fields are the primary owners forced onto the fat interface's mutator; freeing them is the core of the Interface Segregation repair for this repository.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, StructType is not required to expose a no-argument scalar value get()/set(); the container depends only on buffer/aggregation responsibilities and named-field access remains the supported read path.
rubrics.rationale: StructType, the field container, is the second owner forced onto value members it cannot satisfy; removing that obligation is core to the segregated design.

rubrics.criterion: Value fields that genuinely use set()/get() (scalar, array, raw-string, and null-terminated-string fields) still expose set()/get() with their existing value semantics, so call sites that read or write a field's value through StructType keep working.
rubrics.rationale: These owners legitimately implement the value contract and form the contrast with the read-only owners; the repair must keep their value read/write behavior intact across the dependency change.

rubrics.criterion: A shared buffer contract still unifies every field type (value fields, SizeOf*/Pointer* computed fields, and StructType) so computeBufferSize()/toUint8Array() and struct offset/size computations resolve consistently and behave as before.
rubrics.rationale: Buffer shape is a genuinely shared responsibility across all field types; preserving that shared buffer contract keeps struct composition, offsets, and size reporting correct after the split.

rubrics.criterion: The repair removes the throw-stub set() methods that were introduced on the read-only computed fields and on StructType, rather than leaving them behind as dead but still-compiling members.
rubrics.rationale: These stubs exist only to satisfy the merged interface; an incomplete repair that leaves them silently violates cleanup of the injected obligation.

rubrics.criterion: The repair removes the no-argument get() throw guard added to StructType (the injected if (name === undefined) throw path) and restores the named-field accessor without the stub read path.
rubrics.rationale: The StructType no-arg get guard is an injected artifact distinct from the set stubs; it must be removed even if the set family is handled, or the container still carries an unused read path.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not retain a single field interface that still requires both set() and get() of the read-only computed fields and/or StructType (the merged obligation is removed from those owners, not merely supplemented).
rubrics.rationale: Adding a focused value interface without removing the fat members from the shared contract is a plausible but incomplete repair that leaves the Interface Segregation violation in place.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not remove or alter the value members on the value fields in a way that breaks reading or writing field values (e.g. treating the task as removing set()/get() everywhere).
rubrics.rationale: A shortcut that strips set()/get() uniformly would remove the unused members but break the value fields that legitimately need them, regressing callers that read/write field values.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is not partial: it does not leave the smell in any field family (for example fixing SizeOf* but leaving Pointer*, fixing the 8/16/32 families but leaving the 64-bit variants, or fixing the computed fields but leaving StructType).
rubrics.rationale: The obligation spans several distinct field responsibilities; a partial repair that fixes only one family leaves the others still forced onto the fat interface.
